case_study_insert.main_stem: Coastway Travel Holidays (CTH) is a cooperative in the tourism sector, selling coastal package holidays and employing a workforce of 28. Founded in 2011 by Grace Osei, CTH uses a flat organisational structure with democratic leadership, letting member teams vote on customer-service changes. CTH plans to invest $640,000 in a new online booking platform and three coastal tour hubs, financed by a $400,000 ten-year bank loan and $240,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $168,000 a year, a variable cost of $22 a unit and a selling price of $78, and currently produces 15,000 units a year, each a booked holiday. CTH faces two problems: staff turnover has reached 12% and customer complaints about booking errors are rising.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Customer Operations Report — Q2 2025: CTH handled 3,750 holiday bookings last quarter at an average booking value of $78. Online booking errors rose to 41 per month from 23. Customer complaints rose to 38 per month from 22. Satisfaction fell from 4.3 to 3.8 out of 5. Average response time is 14 minutes. A survey of 650 travellers found that 63% would pay $4 more for instant confirmation and 55% book by mobile. Records show 8 of 28 staff have not completed on-the-job training on the digital system; off-the-job training courses cost $230 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Financial Position of Coastway Travel Holidays as at 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Tourism Bulletin (June 2026): (1) The central bank raised the base interest rate from 4.00% to 4.60%, increasing borrowing costs on CTH's variable-rate loan. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 5.5% from $12.20 to $12.87 per hour, raising the wage bill for CTH's 28 staff. (3) Travel fuel and commission costs have risen 9.8% year-on-year, while consumer spending on domestic holidays grew 3.3% and online bookings rose 6.1%.

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages for CTH of using $240,000 retained profit alongside the $400,000 bank loan to fund the booking platform.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Combining $240,000 retained profit with the $400,000 bank loan reduces the amount CTH must borrow for the $640,000 platform, lowering interest and repayments. With fixed costs of $168,000 a year and a $56 contribution on each of 15,000 bookings, keeping debt smaller leaves more cash to run the three tour hubs. The retained profit is immediately available, so the platform can be launched without waiting for further credit approval.

Point 2: Using internal funds keeps control with the cooperative's members rather than a lender, and no collateral is tied up beyond the loan already agreed. It also leaves a reserve for the 12% staff turnover and the $230 per employee digital-training cost, so the existing service is not neglected while the new system is built. The mix therefore balances expansion with the working capital needed to cut the 38 monthly complaints. A cooperative keeps those savings available to its 28 member teams.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage of combining retained profit with debt identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to CTH's $640,000 platform, booking economics and staffing.

questions.question_text: CTH is launching its new online booking platform. Consider television advertising, direct mail, or social media influencer marketing. Which should CTH choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Television advertising: TV gives very wide reach and could quickly make travellers aware of the new platform, but airtime is expensive for a cooperative with a $400,000 loan and $168,000 fixed costs. Many viewers do not book coastal holidays, so much of the spend is wasted, and a 28-employee business cannot afford a national campaign.

Direct mail: Sending offers to existing customer lists is cheap and targeted, and could help recover satisfaction from 3.8 to 4.3. Response rates are low, printing and postage add up, and it will not reach the 55% of 650 surveyed travellers who book by mobile, limiting its ability to drive use of the new platform.

Social media influencer marketing: Travel influencers can demonstrate instant confirmation directly to mobile-first travellers and to the 63% of surveyed travellers willing to pay $4 more for it. Engagement is trackable and costs less than television. Results take time and depend on choosing credible influencers, but targeting is precise.

Recommendation: CTH should choose social media influencer marketing. It reaches the mobile booking segment in the survey, supports the $4 instant-confirmation premium and is far cheaper than television. Television is rejected as unaffordable and untargeted, and direct mail as too slow and narrow to promote a digital platform, so a small email follow-up to existing customers should supplement it. CTH can reuse influencer clips in its own app and measure results against the 38 complaints and 14-minute response time, which television and direct mail cannot match for a cooperative with a $400,000 loan.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited outline of the three promotional options with minimal reference to CTH.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discussion of at least two options with some application to CTH's platform launch.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three options with a justified recommendation explaining why television and direct mail are rejected.

questions.question_text: CTH's staff turnover has reached 12% and booking errors are rising. Explain two benefits for CTH of using democratic leadership to improve staff motivation.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership lets CTH's 28 member teams vote on changes to the booking process, so staff who see the 41 monthly errors first-hand can propose fixes. This involvement satisfies social and esteem needs and raises job satisfaction, helping to cut the 12% turnover and protect the 3,750 bookings handled last quarter and the $78 booking value.

Point 2: Consulting employees improves decisions because those entering the bookings know where errors occur, reducing the 38 monthly complaints and the 14-minute response time. Greater commitment lowers recruitment costs and the $230 per employee digital-training bill, protecting the $56 contribution on each booking while the $400,000 loan is repaid and the new platform beds in. Voting on changes suits a cooperative whose members expect a say, so new booking routines are accepted faster. With 12% turnover, keeping 28 team members engaged is cheaper than repeated recruitment and training on the $640,000 platform.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of democratic leadership identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to CTH's turnover, errors and training costs.

questions.question_text: CTH must train 8 staff to use the new online booking platform. Consider on-the-job training or off-the-job training with a course. Which should CTH choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Learning the platform on the job with experienced colleagues is specific to CTH's own system, costs no fees and keeps all 8 staff handling the 3,750 bookings while they learn. It can reduce the 41 booking errors quickly. Drawbacks are that trainers are also working, so response times may lengthen, and informal shortcuts can spread unless managers check accuracy; certification is limited if members want proof of competence.

Off-the-job training: The course at $230 per employee costs $1,840 for 8 staff — small against the $640,000 investment — and gives structured digital skills with a certificate. It takes 8 of 28 staff away from bookings at a time when satisfaction is 3.8, and generic content may not match CTH's system, so on-the-job follow-up would still be needed.

Decision: CTH should choose on-the-job training with a short certified course later. It is cheaper, system-specific and avoids losing 8 workers while errors and 12% turnover already strain the team; full off-the-job training is rejected because the $1,840 fee and lost booking capacity are harder to justify than practical coaching on the actual platform. Member teams should check a sample of bookings daily so the 41 errors do not rise, and any trainee making repeated mistakes should be paired with an experienced colleague. If formal proof is later wanted, the $1,840 course can come from retained profit without increasing the $400,000 loan, keeping the 3,750 bookings and 3.8 satisfaction score protected while the $640,000 platform and three tour hubs go live.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to CTH.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analysis of benefits and drawbacks of both methods in the context of CTH's booking errors.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods with a justified decision covering cost, disruption and relevance to CTH's platform.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how CTH's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $168,000 ÷ ($78 − $22) = $168,000 ÷ $56 = 3,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 3,000 holiday bookings a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $78 − $22 = $56. Answer: contribution per unit is $56.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways CTH's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare 3,000-unit break-even with actual output of 15,000 bookings: the margin of safety is 12,000 bookings, showing the platform and three hubs can be introduced with little loss risk.
2. Use the $56 contribution to test pricing: the $4 instant-confirmation charge would lift contribution to $60, which can be checked against the 63% of 650 surveyed travellers who support it.
3. Check loan capacity: only 3,000 bookings are needed to break even, so the $400,000 repayment is coverable and managers can set monthly booking targets to protect the cushion.
4. Benchmark unit cost: $168,000 ÷ 15,000 units + $22 = $33.20 a booking, a figure to monitor so the 9.8% fuel and commission inflation is caught before it erodes the $56 contribution.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 3,000 bookings | (ii) Contribution per unit = $56 | (iii) Four uses: 12,000-booking margin of safety, $4 instant-confirmation premium modelling, $400,000 loan feasibility and $33.20 unit-cost benchmarking.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark per valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate CTH's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has CTH's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.50 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.40 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 1.33 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 1.23 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $12,000 inventories + $65,000 trade receivables + $28,000 cash = $105,000. 2025 current assets = $15,000 + $96,000 + $15,000 = $126,000. 2024: $105,000 ÷ $70,000 = 1.50; 2025: $126,000 ÷ $90,000 = 1.40. Excluding inventories: 2024 ($105,000 − $12,000) ÷ $70,000 = $93,000 ÷ $70,000 = 1.33; 2025 ($126,000 − $15,000) ÷ $90,000 = $111,000 ÷ $90,000 = 1.23.

Evaluation: Liquidity has deteriorated. The first measure fell from 1.50 to 1.40 because current liabilities grew from $70,000 to $90,000 faster than current assets, and the second fell from 1.33 to 1.23. Cash dropped from $28,000 to $15,000 while trade receivables rose from $65,000 to $96,000, so more of CTH's short-term wealth is tied up with customers at the very time it is spending $640,000 on a booking platform. With a $400,000 loan to service, a smaller cash buffer increases risk if those receivables are paid late.

Conclusion: CTH's financial position has not improved; it has weakened. Both measures are lower and the fall in cash is the main reason, so CTH should tighten credit control and rebuild cash before committing further funds to the three tour hubs. The $240,000 retained profit in the platform should be replenished before more borrowing is considered, because $15,000 of cash is a thin buffer against the $400,000 loan.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates both ratios for 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years plus detailed evaluation of cash, receivables and liabilities and a justified conclusion on deterioration.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for CTH of charging $4 more for instant booking confirmation.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: The survey of 650 travellers found that 63% would pay $4 more for instant confirmation and 55% already book by mobile, so the charge can lift contribution from $56 towards $60 a booking. That helps cover $168,000 fixed costs and the $400,000 loan, and could reduce the 38 monthly complaints and improve the 3.8 satisfaction score.

Disadvantage: Instant confirmation requires reliable technology, and failures could increase the 41 booking errors rather than reduce them. Competitors may offer confirmation free, so a $4 charge could deter the 55% mobile bookers and cost bookings; any improvement must also survive the 9.8% rise in fuel and commission costs. Instant confirmation fits the 55% who book by mobile and can differentiate the cooperative, helping reverse the fall in satisfaction to 3.8. If the $4 charge is accepted, contribution rises from $56 to $60 and the 38 complaints may fall, but reliable technology must come first.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development using CTH's survey, costs and service data.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 4.60%, the 5.5% minimum wage increase and the 9.8% rise in travel fuel and commission costs will affect CTH. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.00% to 4.60%): If CTH's $400,000 bank loan is variable-rate, the extra interest is 0.60% of $400,000 = $2,400 a year (0.006 × $400,000). That is small beside fixed costs of $168,000 a year and would be zero if the loan were fixed. Higher rates might slow consumer spending on domestic holidays, but the direct finance cost is modest and can be capped by fixing the rate.

Minimum wage increase (5.5%, to $12.87 per hour): CTH has a workforce of 28, so the rise lifts the wage bill and cannot be avoided. The insert does not give hours worked or individual pay, so a defensible annual total cannot be invented; the fair test is productivity of 15,000 bookings ÷ 28 staff = 535.71 bookings per worker. If that holds, the higher wage is spread across more bookings; with 12% turnover it could raise unit labour cost and cut the $56 contribution.

Fuel and commission inflation (9.8%): The $22 variable cost per booking is not decomposed in the insert, so only a bound is honest: if the whole $22 rose 9.8%, that is 0.098 × $22 = $2.16 a booking, and at 15,000 bookings about $32,400 a year. It applies to every booking and directly threatens the contribution that funds the $640,000 platform; the $4 confirmation charge cannot cover all of it.

Conclusion: The 9.8% rise in fuel and commission costs will have the greatest impact because it compounds across all 15,000 bookings and erodes the $56 contribution, while the interest rise is a bounded $2,400 and the wage rise can be absorbed if 535.71 bookings per worker is maintained.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the three external changes with limited application to CTH.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two changes on CTH's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three changes in CTH's context with a justified greatest-impact judgment and reasons why the others are smaller.
